plan.summary: GB-55: `outfeed clean` & `outfeed prune` Workspace Cache Hygiene
plan.design_markdown:
# GB-55: `outfeed clean` & `outfeed prune` Workspace Cache Hygiene

> **Status:** InProgress  
> **Target Scope:** `outfeed` (`outfeed-core`, `outfeed-cli`, `outfeed-mcp`)  
> **Key Invariants:**  
> 1. Hard 250 LOC rule on all `.rs` files.  
> 2. Zero-panic safety: no `.unwrap()` / `.expect()` in production library paths (`thiserror`).  
> 3. Safe-by-default: `outfeed clean` cleans `target/debug` while strictly preserving `target/release/` and release binaries.  
> 4. Accurate disk reporting in `--dry-run` modes.  
> 5. Age-based test executable pruning in `outfeed prune`.  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement

The `gaugeblock` meta-harness configures a shared build directory (`target-dir = "target"` in `.cargo/config.toml`) to prevent 10 separate workspaces from compiling redundant copies of third-party crates.

While this saves significant compile time, full test executions and continuous development rapidly balloon `target/debug` to 15–30+ GB with stale test executables, `.rlib`s, and incremental compilation hashes.

Standard `cargo clean` is too blunt—it wipes `target/` entirely, deleting optimized release binaries and forcing lengthy re-compilation.

`GB-55` adds centralized workspace cache hygiene to `outfeed`:
1. **`outfeed clean`**: Selectively purges `target/debug` build artifacts and test binaries while preserving `target/release`.
2. **`outfeed clean --dry-run`**: Audits and reports exact disk usage broken down by component (`debug`, `release`, `doc`, total reclaimable).
3. **`outfeed clean --all`**: Full target directory clean across meta-harness and member checkouts.
4. **`outfeed clean --doc`**: Purges only documentation artifacts in `target/doc`.
5. **`outfeed prune [--keep-days <N>]`**: Selectively prunes test binaries and artifacts older than N days (default 3) in `target/debug/deps`.

---

## 2. Architecture & File Layout

```text
outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/src/
├── clean.rs          # Core disk calculation, selective clean, and age-based pruning (<200 LOC)
├── model.rs          # CleanOpts, PruneOpts, CleanReport, DiskUsage
└── lib.rs            # Re-exports clean module

outfeed/crates/outfeed-cli/src/
├── commands/
│   ├── clean.rs      # Subcommand handler for outfeed clean and prune (<100 LOC)
│   └── mod.rs        # Re-export clean handler
└── args.rs           # CleanArgs and PruneArgs Clap definitions

outfeed/crates/outfeed-mcp/src/
├── schema.rs         # outfeed_clean schema definition
└── dispatch.rs       # MCP tool dispatcher

outfeed/crates/outfeed-core/tests/
└── clean_tests.rs    # Unit tests for size calculation, dry-run, and selective pruning
```

---

## 3. Data Contracts

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DiskUsage {
    pub debug_bytes: u64,
    pub release_bytes: u64,
    pub doc_bytes: u64,
    pub other_bytes: u64,
    pub total_bytes: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CleanReport {
    pub initial_usage: DiskUsage,
    pub reclaimed_bytes: u64,
    pub paths_removed: Vec<String>,
    pub dry_run: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CleanOpts {
    pub clean_all: bool,
    pub clean_doc: bool,
    pub clean_release: bool,
    pub dry_run: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PruneOpts {
    pub keep_days: u32,
    pub dry_run: bool,
}
```

---

## 4. Verification & Dogfooding Gate

1. **Tier 1:** `cargo check -p outfeed-core`
2. **Tier 2:** `cargo fmt --check -p outfeed-core`, `cargo clippy -p outfeed-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p outfeed-core`
3. **Tier 3:** `cargo test --workspace --manifest-path outfeed/Cargo.toml`
4. **Tier 4 / Dogfooding:** Run `outfeed clean --dry-run` and `outfeed clean` to reclaim disk space safely.

task.title: Add outfeed reserve: check, scaffold and publish namespace placeholders
task.description: Packaging is meant to be outfeed's end to end, so reserving crate names on crates.io belongs here rather than in a per-repository shell script. crates.io has no reservation API: a name is held only by publishing a version, and a published version can be yanked but never deleted, so the first release is permanent. Every project therefore needs the same three steps and currently rewrites them by hand; aerofoil's scripts/reserve-namespaces.sh is the reference implementation, written for that purpose (ADR-0007 there).
acceptance_criteria: outfeed reserve check lists free/taken per name from the registry API, read only, exit non-zero when any name is taken; outfeed reserve scaffold writes standalone placeholder crates at 0.1.0-alpha.1 into a gitignored staging directory, each declaring an empty workspace table and excluded by the parent workspace; outfeed reserve publish requires explicit confirmation, skips names already taken, honours the reset timestamp in a 429 body, continues past an individual failure and reports what stayed unpublished, exit non-zero if any remain; placeholder versions are alpha only, never beta; park an explicit outfeed publish command that refuses a dirty tree; MCP tool parity with the existing outfeed_* surface; the sibling shell scripts reduce to wrappers around the outfeed command

description:
Packaging is meant to be outfeed's end to end, so reserving crate names on crates.io belongs here rather than in a per-repository shell script. crates.io has no reservation API: a name is held only by publishing a version, and a published version can be yanked but never deleted, so the first release is permanent. Every project therefore needs the same three steps and currently rewrites them by hand; aerofoil's scripts/reserve-namespaces.sh is the reference implementation, written for that purpose (ADR-0007 there). Measured against crates.io on 2026-11-04 while reserving eight names: a burst of five new crates is accepted in seconds, then the window closes for roughly ten minutes per crate; the 429 body names the exact reopening time (honouring it succeeded on the first retry where a fixed sleep had collided twice); metadata including the repository URL is immutable per version, so placeholders must be scaffolded with the final URLs; and a staging directory inside a workspace needs both an empty workspace table in each placeholder and an exclude entry in the parent or cargo tries to enrol them as members.

DOGFOOD SCOPE 2026-11-06 (pulled forward by the owner ahead of the next release; priority raised to P1). Measured against the crates.io API today: of the 51 package names in the suite, exactly five are unreserved and therefore block a publish - gaugeblock-security, gaugeblock-workspace, miter-analysis, miter-inventory, miter-polyglot. Every other name resolves 200, including gaugeblock-common, gaugeblock-contracts, gaugeblock-git, gaugeblock-mcp, miter-ast, miter-engine and all product crates. Those five are the first real input for `outfeed reserve check`, which is what makes this dogfooding rather than a smoke test.

SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT: reserve only once the names are final. A published version can be yanked but never deleted, so reserving miter-polyglot and then moving it to common as gaugeblock-polyglot burns a permanent name for nothing. GB-204 decision D3 (placement of the split-out crates) must be resolved before `reserve publish` runs against these five. `reserve check` and `reserve scaffold` carry no such constraint and can be built and dogfooded immediately.

Second-order benefit worth noting: gaugeblock-workspace and gaugeblock-security are already consumed by six member repositories that only build because the harness [patch.crates-io] table maps them to local paths. Until those two are published, no member builds standalone from a clean checkout - which is the Law 2 standalone-value claim, not just a release chore.

STEP 1 DONE 2026-11-06: `outfeed reserve check|scaffold|publish` ships in outfeed-core and the CLI (commits d2f4df9, b962cf9).

Built on what already existed rather than beside it: the 429 body parsing and countdown come from rate_limit.rs, the sparse-index sharding from index_poll.rs. One addition was needed: IndexLookup separates "the registry answered 404" from "the registry did not answer", because reporting a name free after a timeout would be a claim the tool cannot support - unknown is not free and exits non-zero like taken does.

Dogfooded against the real registry with the installed binary:
- check on the five unreserved names: 5 free, 0 taken, 0 unknown, exit 0.
- check on gaugeblock-contracts and storypole-core: both taken (0.1.0-alpha.1 placeholder and 0.1.0-beta.5), exit non-zero with "nothing was published".
- scaffold gaugeblock-inventory with --repo-override name=https://github.com/gaugeblock/common wrote a placeholder at 0.1.0-alpha.1 carrying that repository URL, which is the path D3 needs.
- cargo metadata inside the placeholder reports workspace_root = the placeholder itself and exactly one member, so the empty [workspace] table does prevent enrollment.

Two defects the dogfood found and fixed: the exclude hint compared a joined absolute path against the manifest's relative pattern and warned about an entry that was already present, and reserve-staging/ was not gitignored in this repository (the root harness ignore does not reach into it).

STILL OPEN on this ticket: MCP tool parity with the outfeed_* surface, the sibling shell scripts reduced to wrappers, and an explicit outfeed publish that refuses a dirty tree. reserve publish is implemented and guarded by --confirm but has not been run: names must be final first (D3).

That is the whole of what reservation does, and it is worth being precise: it claims the names. It does NOT make the members build standalone, because consumers pin 0.1.0-beta.1 (gaugeblock-*) and 0.1.0-beta.4 (miter-*), and those versions do not exist yet - the placeholders are alpha.1 by design. Independent building arrives when the real crates publish at beta, which is what the reservation unblocked. GB-254 is the gate that would have caught the gap.

Still open on this ticket: MCP tool parity, the sibling shell scripts as wrappers, and a dirty-tree guard on publish.
